# Modal for LabQuorum: recommendation

**Not Modal for the deadline.** Use the AWS Free plan Ubuntu EC2 approach in `docs/build/remote-host.md:5-6,11-34`, subject to account, eligible shape and credit confirmation. Modal can run Docker in a VM Sandbox and can expose SSH, but its 24-hour Sandbox lifetime forces at least two disruptive replacements over 60 hours. Restoring the stack, database and Switch's tmux sidecar safely is unproven. Splitting services across Modal adds engineering and database risk. Estimated EC2 setup is 1.5-3 hours after activation versus at least 8-16 hours for a credible Modal trial. These are estimates, not measured deployments. AWS's reported $100 initial credit and Free plan duration are cited at `docs/build/remote-host.md:13,54-56`; actual shape, capacity and charges remain UNVERIFIED.

Research checked 2026-11-05 IST against the linked current official pages and pinned Switch v0.40.1. No deployment was tested. Deadline: 2026-11-07 23:59 IST.

## Switch remote-host contract

Pinned reference paths below are relative to `C:/Users/Nikhil/.claude/jobs/85ca08fa/tmp/ref/switch-v0.40.1/`.

| Requirement | Modal assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, x86-64, controlled shell | **Partial.** `Image.from_registry("ubuntu:24.04")`, `Sandbox.create(..., runtime="vm")` and `sb.exec(...)` are documented. Exact Switch host checks and OS behavior are UNVERIFIED. [Sandboxes](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandboxes), [images](https://modal.com/docs/guide/existing-images); `docs/official/deploy/host-remotely.md:19-24,41-46`. |
| SSH key, alias, sudo | **Partial.** Sandbox `unencrypted_ports` exposes raw TCP; Modal explicitly demonstrates `sshd` and key authentication through `modal.forward(..., unencrypted=True)` in a Function. That is raw tunnel transport, not plaintext SSH: SSH itself encrypts. The endpoint is public and its random host/port must be secured and rediscovered. Sandbox-specific sshd, sudo, host-key verification and Console alias onboarding are UNVERIFIED. [Sandbox API](https://modal.com/docs/sdk/py/latest/Sandbox), [SSH example](https://modal.com/docs/sdk/py/latest/forward); `docs/official/deploy/host-remotely.md:24-27,54-58`. |
| Docker and Compose | **Partial.** Modal explicitly says "Use the VM runtime to run Docker in a Sandbox" and demonstrates `dockerd` and `docker run`; gVisor is a different userspace-kernel runtime, so do not assume Docker works there. Compose plugin installation and this complete stack under VM Sandbox are UNVERIFIED. [Sandboxes](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandboxes), [runtime isolation](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-networking); `docs/official/deploy/host-remotely.md:29,46`; `deploy/local/standalone-docker-compose.yml:61-80,142-149`. |
| tmux, Node, Claude CLI, repo | **Partial.** Install in the Ubuntu image and run via shell in principle; actual installation, authentication and Switch's sidecar checks are UNVERIFIED. Switch requires tmux, Node 18+ and provider CLI; persistent Windows Console agents require a POSIX host. `docs/official/deploy/host-remotely.md:60-68,84-94`; `docs/build/switch-facts.md:98-104`. |
| Survive laptop/Console disconnect and stay up | **Partial / no for 60 hours continuously.** A running Sandbox is independent of the laptop, but defaults to five minutes and has a maximum lifetime of **24 hours**. Optional `idle_timeout` can terminate it earlier; a running exec command or open tunnel connection counts as active. Switch's tmux sidecar must be relaunched after a host restart. [Sandboxes](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandboxes); `docs/official/deploy/host-remotely.md:7-9,80-90`. |
| Durable filesystem and database | **Partial.** Sandbox filesystem snapshots can seed a replacement, including `/var/lib/docker` in VM Sandboxes, but are point-in-time images, not a live database backup or process continuation. Memory snapshots are alpha, close TCP connections, terminate the source, and have exec/background-process restrictions. Clean shutdown, database-consistent backup, restore and sidecar re-onboarding are required; exact reliability is UNVERIFIED. [Snapshots](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-snapshots), [Sandboxes](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandboxes). |

**Bottom line for contract:** a short-lived experimental SSH host is plausible, not a dependable 60-hour Switch remote host. `encrypted_ports` supplies TLS tunnels and `unencrypted_ports` raw TCP; `sandbox.tunnels()` retrieves addresses. `modal.forward` is an alternative Function tunnel API. Neither removes lifetime or recovery work. [Sandbox API](https://modal.com/docs/sdk/py/latest/Sandbox), [tunnels](https://modal.com/docs/guide/tunnels).

## Current pricing and limits

Modal's [pricing](https://modal.com/pricing), checked 2026-11-05, says Starter includes **"$30 / month free credits"** per workspace, for Function and Sandbox CPU, memory and GPU compute. It includes three seats, 100 containers, 10 concurrent GPUs, 1 TiB/month Volume storage and 1 TiB/month egress. Shared Endpoint token charges are excluded; excess compute and other non-included use are billable. The listed Function CPU rate is $0.0000131 per physical core-second and RAM $0.00000222 per GiB-second; one physical core is stated as two vCPUs. Sandbox non-preemptible rates are $0.00003942 and $0.00000667 respectively, approximately 3x. CPU and RAM are each billed at the higher of reservation and actual use; reservations accrue even when idle. [Resources](https://modal.com/docs/guide/resources), [Sandbox resources](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-resources).

For 60 hours, 216,000 seconds, with fixed average billed resources and no location multiplier, illustrative compute only:

- Mattermost Function, 0.5 core / 2 GiB: `216000 * (0.5 * 0.0000131 + 2 * 0.00000222) = $2.37`.
- Decomposed core, Gateway and Mattermost Functions together, 1 core / 4 GiB: `216000 * (1 * 0.0000131 + 4 * 0.00000222) = $4.75`.
- MCP Function, 0.125 core / 0.5 GiB: `216000 * (0.125 * 0.0000131 + 0.5 * 0.00000222) = $0.59`.
- Four agents plus controller in VM Sandbox, 1 core / 4 GiB: `216000 * (1 * 0.00003942 + 4 * 0.00000667) = $14.28`.
- Whole stack and four agents in a VM Sandbox, 1 core / 8 GiB: `216000 * (1 * 0.00003942 + 8 * 0.00000667) = $20.04`.

These are scenario assumptions, not measured sizing or a performance guarantee; 60 hours requires Sandbox replacements. The decomposed $4.75 excludes external PostgreSQL, agent host and MCP; adding the separate agent and MCP scenarios gives roughly $19.62, plus database and integration costs. Do not add these to the whole-stack estimate. Image builds, bursts, backups, external database, Claude usage and paid overages can increase costs. The ledger is not safe merely because its compute estimate is low. A 1.75x narrow-region multiplier would make the whole-stack estimate about $35.07, exceeding one workspace's $30 credit before extras. [Region pricing](https://modal.com/docs/guide/region-selection).

Modal offers `ap-south` container selection and Mumbai `ap-south` Function routing. A narrow container-region selection costs 1.75x, broad `ap` 1.15x; unspecified location has no selection multiplier. Routing defaults to Virginia for Functions, while Sandboxes mostly connect directly. Actual India capacity, latency and VM availability are UNVERIFIED. [Region selection](https://modal.com/docs/guide/region-selection).

## Component options

**(a) Mattermost web app: feasible as a prototype, 4-8 hours**, plus external PostgreSQL and testing. `@modal.web_server` can start an HTTP service and supports WebSockets; Modal requires concurrency configuration for simultaneous inputs. It does not support WebSocket permessage-deflate, and standard Web Functions enforce a 150-second HTTP request timeout with redirect behavior. Mattermost compatibility, long-lived socket behavior, bridge callbacks and reconnects are UNVERIFIED. Persistent uploads need a supported external store or a carefully tested persistence design. Idle Functions scale to zero by default, with cold starts; `min_containers=1` keeps capacity warm at a cost but does not guarantee uninterrupted service. [Web Functions](https://modal.com/docs/guide/webhooks), [timeouts](https://modal.com/docs/guide/webhook-timeouts), [cold starts](https://modal.com/docs/guide/cold-start); pinned `deploy/local/standalone-docker-compose.yml:142-168,180-185`.

**(b) Decomposed Switch stack: technically plausible but high-risk, 16-32+ hours.** Core, Gateway, init/seeding and Mattermost need recreated startup order, reachable addresses, authentication, callbacks and an external durable PostgreSQL. Switch requires one core replica; its database stores critical state. `Image.from_registry` accepts public amd64 images, so the pinned Mattermost and Postgres references are candidates, but compatible entrypoints, Python for Functions, users, startup commands and behavior require testing. Modal ignores image `USER`; importing an image does not reproduce Compose networking or volumes. PostgreSQL on a Modal Volume is not established as safe; use managed or VM-hosted PostgreSQL with backups. [Image requirements](https://modal.com/docs/guide/existing-images); `docs/official/deploy/self-host.md:52-67,75-106`; `deploy/local/standalone-docker-compose.yml:61-80,87-90,142-149`.

**(c) MCP server and SQLite ledger: compute feasible, ledger persistence unsafe without redesign, 8-16+ hours.** Switch's MCP integration currently expects a process and stdio; an HTTP Modal endpoint requires verified transport and client configuration changes. Modal Volumes require commits for durable visibility, reload for external changes, and do not support distributed file locking; concurrent changes to one file are last-writer-wins. Therefore multiple replicas cannot safely share SQLite for booking transactions, and a single writer still needs verified SQLite locking, WAL/checkpoint, crash recovery and commit durability before acknowledging bookings. Local SQLite transaction commit alone is not demonstrated to durably commit the Volume. Use a suitable external transactional database or keep the ledger on the EC2 host. [Volume API](https://modal.com/docs/sdk/py/latest/Volume), [Sandbox file access](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-files); `docs/build/switch-facts.md:17-19`. SQLite-on-Volume support and exact MCP compatibility are **UNVERIFIED**.

**(d) Four Claude sessions: possible in a VM Sandbox, 8-16+ hours**, with SSH onboarding, secrets and controller installation. They can outlive laptop disconnect, but will be interrupted at each Sandbox replacement; tmux processes and network connections do not simply survive a filesystem snapshot. Restore and re-register/restart the sidecar, test Claude authentication and reconnect, and protect keys. A Sandbox on its own does not supply the Switch controller. `docs/official/deploy/host-remotely.md:84-94`; [snapshots](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-snapshots).

## Terms and practical decision

Modal explicitly documents SSH tunnels and Docker VM Sandboxes, and advertises web servers. Its [terms](https://modal.com/legal/terms) apply generally; a special prohibition or permission for this exact long-running Switch/SSH use is **UNVERIFIED**, not inferred from the examples. Account eligibility, workloads, exact charges, upstream Claude terms and all integration tests remain open. The Starter credit is shared by the workspace, not multiplied by two members. Inviting a teammate requires a verified account, including a payment method according to [workspace documentation](https://modal.com/docs/guide/workspaces). Since no Modal component is recommended for this deadline, no Modal deployment runbook or signup is necessary; follow the cited EC2 runbook and test all four agents and a booking before migration.
